items.title: Exim — Multiple Mail Server Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Classification: Important, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 7.5, CVEs: CVE-2026-94054, CVE-2026-94055, CVE-2026-94056, CVE-2026-94057, Summary: Multiple security vulnerabilities have been disclosed in Exim affecting Proxy Protocol processing, TLS handling and SMTP message processing. The vulnerabilities are addressed in Exim 4.100.1. The most significant issue, CVE-2026-94054, is an out-of-bounds write that can be triggered over the network without authentication when Proxy Protocol is enabled and an attacker controls the connecting proxy. CVE-2026-94056 can disclose uninitialized stack memory under the same Proxy Protocol prerequisite. CVE-2026-94057 is an SMTP smuggling vulnerability involving crafted data following rejection during SMTP DATA processing. CVE-2026-94055 is a use-after-free affecting installations using certain non-default GnuTLS settings. The vulnerabilities have significant configuration or attack-position prerequisites, reducing exposure compared with an unconditional unauthenticated vulnerability in a default Exim installation.

items.title: D-Link Routers — Administrative Takeover and Command Injection Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Temporary Fix, Exploit Maturity: Functional, CVSSv4.0: 9.4, CVEs: CVE-2026-93958, CVE-2026-94036, Summary: Security vulnerabilities affecting multiple D-Link router models can result in administrative compromise or command execution, and public exploit material is available. CVE-2026-93958 affects the D-Link R95 and allows OS command injection through the DHMAPI interface. The attack can be performed remotely and can result in execution of arbitrary commands on the router, but exploitation requires high privileges. CVE-2026-94036 affects the DIR-X1860 and DIR-X1860Z routerd/ubus interface. An unauthenticated attacker with access to the local network can exploit insufficient access controls to perform administrative operations, including changing the router administrator password. The DIR-X1860 has reached end of life and should be replaced. D-Link has released corrected firmware for the supported DIR-X1860Z.

items.title: An undercover Google analyst infiltrated a notorious supply-chain hacking gang
items.summary: Before two of its alleged members were arrested and charged in Australia last month, the hacker group known as TeamPCP carried out a hacking spree unlike any other in history. It tainted hundreds of open-source programs with its malware, stole developer accounts to perpetuate that software supply-chain hacking, and even released a Dune-themed self-spreading worm to automate the process, ultimately breaching more than a thousand companies. Now Google’s threat intelligence group has revealed that during a key moment of TeamPCP’s rampage, the company’s own undercover researcher had infiltrated the group—allowing Google to monitor the hacking spree from the inside, warn breach targets, and even help disrupt the group’s attempts to exploit those victims.

items.title: REDCap — Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
items.summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 9.8, CVEs: CVE-2026-90817, Summary: A critical remote code execution vulnerability has been disclosed in REDCap. CVE-2026-90817 affects survey passthrough routing and Data Import processing and can allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the REDCap server. Exploitation requires knowledge of a valid public survey hash. An attacker with such a hash can manipulate HTTP requests to reach an unintended controller route from the public survey context and supply a crafted file path or stream parameter during import processing. The vulnerability affects REDCap versions from 13.3.0. No evidence of active exploitation has currently been identified.

items.title: AI coding agents' 0-click RCE flaw could hand attackers keys to the kingdom
items.summary: A zero-click vulnerability that allows remote code execution affects all of the major AI coding agents - Anthropic’s Claude Code, OpenAI’s Codex, Google's Gemini CLI, Microsoft’s Copilot, and Microsoft-owned GitHub Copilot - and could give attackers full access to every asset and piece of data that the agent can reach, researchers say. The exploit, dubbed “Plugin4Shell,” is a “first-of-its-kind AI supply-chain attack,” according to threat hunters at Air, a security startup focused on protecting enterprise AI agents.

items.title: Suricata — Multiple Security Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Classification: Severe, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 9.4, CVEs: CVE-2026-94083, CVE-2026-94084, Summary: The Open Information Security Foundation (OISF) has released Suricata 8.0.7 to address a large number of security vulnerabilities. The release includes vulnerabilities that OISF rates Critical and is described by OISF as the Suricata release with the highest number of vulnerability reports to date. Two newly assigned vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-94083 and CVE-2026-94084, affect HTTP/2 processing. CVE-2026-94083 is a type-confusion vulnerability that can result in an invalid free when processing a crafted DoH2 protocol upgrade. The affected DoH2 functionality is enabled by default in Suricata 8.x. CVE-2026-94084 is a use-after-free that can occur when HTTP response headers are inspected using particular rule and transform combinations. Suricata 8.0.7 contains numerous additional security fixes whose CVE identifiers remain pending. Organizations should therefore upgrade based on the security release itself rather than waiting for all CVE assignments. Suricata 7 has reached end of life.

items.title: New RatHat Android malware uses AI to automate device control
items.summary: A new Android malware called RatHat has been discovered, targeting users with an AI-powered subsystem that helps operators remotely navigate compromised devices. Zimperium zLabs researchers analyzed the malware and believe it is linked to threat actors from China after finding it using LLM prompts written in Chinese. The researchers say the malware is distributed through malvertising, SMS, and phishing sites promoting APK downloads from outside Google Play.

items.title: ShinyHunters hacks Clop leak site, threatens to extort ransomware gang
items.summary: The ShinyHunters extortion gang breached the Clop (aka Cl0p) ransomware operation's data leak site, defacing the Tor site and allegedly stealing server data and the private keys for its onion service. The attack began Friday night when ShinyHunters exploited what they claim is an unauthenticated file upload vulnerability in Grav CMS, which they used to upload a small text file to Clop's site.
items.summary_html:
